Farmers exploited

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
....how to kick a farmer when he is down.

Unique Selling Point:
The story of a district where farmers are exploited to the maximum because they are in a financially vulnerable situation because of a 9-year-long drought.

Summary:
In a huge area north of Bloemfontein (Bultfontein, Hoopstad, Wesselsbron) has had an incredibly severe drought for several years, and many farmers depleted all their reserves and got into serious financial trouble. The Government refused to help as did the various agricultural organizations. Many farmers now sit with a huge massive debt burden the vultures are circling, because there is a lot of money to be made – legally and illegally. The banks are foreclosing, all kinds of scamsters take advantage of farmers in financial trouble. Dozens of farmers have lost their family farms and for some the only way out is suicide.

Further information:
HOW TO KICK A FARMER WHEN HE IS DOWN
In a huge area North of Bloemfontein (Bultfontein, Hoopstad, Wesselsbron) has had an incredibly severe drought for several years, and many farmers depleted all their reserves, and got into serious financial trouble. The Government refused to help. Many farmers now sit with a huge massive debt burden the vultures are circling, because there is a lot of money to be made – legally and illegally. It is playing out in the following ways:
• The major banks are liquidating farmers left right and centre. Then the farms are being sold for a fraction of their value. Christo Snyman farms and implements with a value of R40 million were sold for less than R10 million. The Banking Association of SA even told them that the banks got together and colluded to liquidate the farmers. FNB is in the forefront of all of this despite new legislation and prior promises and many meetings with people like Christo. In all of this liquidators and liquidating attorney in Bloemfontein are having a ball of a time.

• A Bultfontein Awareness Committee was started in 2018 and negotiated with the banks, and despite concrete plans of how to save many farms and livelihoods, the pleas to the banks went unheeded.

• Good rains fell last year and in a last-ditch effort to save themselves many farmers used private money to plant an the crops are looking promising. However, FNB has now stationed armed guards on many farms, to prevent farmers from harvesting crops, because they owe the bank money. They want to have it harvested themselves to sell.

• Under the severe financial pressure, a number of farmers have committed suicide.

• In recent months a number of unscrupulous characters and charlatans appeared with promises of financial assistance, and many farmers who are in danger of losing everything to the banks, fell for these schemes, losing more millions in the process. For example:

o Ithuba Bank and Europlaw asked farmers 6% of every R100 000 they wanted to borrow as an admin fee. Some farmers paid between R1,6 mil and R1,8 mil in advance and the money in yet to arrive.

o An evangelist, Louis Gerber of the Community Chests Circles Association got 1000 farmers to pay him R350 rand and R60 per month to get shares in the profit of the sale of 178 tons of gold which came into the country in 1965. The very same gold Tokyo Sexwale talked about.

o Universal Venture Capital collected R3500 from farmers as an admin fee to obtains loans, but nothing happened.
It seems it is a story of incredible hardship for a huge farming community and how banks and unscrupulous operators seem to be kicking them when they are down.

Interviewees
o Christo Snyman, who lost everything and who is the Chair of the Bultfontein Awareness Committee christo@teamgap.co.za
o 2 other farmers who are in dire straits.
o “Evangelist” Louis Gerber of the Community Chests Circles Association
o Andre Vorster CEO of Europlaw or Hanno Bekker, manager at Europlaw
o Coenie Fourie -- Bultfontein Awareness Committee


Extra Budget Items:
The story will have to be shot on location in the Bultfontein area. Travel by car to the area and one or two nights accommodation.

Script:


V/O:
Coenie Fourie and his son Stefan have come to a small family cemetery on Stefan’s farm. Vandals have stolen the steel fence that used to surround the resting place of their forebears.

They have come to say goodbye, because in a few days’ time, this farm will be auctioned off to a stranger, to settle their debt with a bank.

We joined Stefan on a last walkabout on Wonderfontein – the farm where he grew up. He spoke of his love of the land … and of loss.

Stefan:
My oupagrootjie, en my oupa en my pa het almal hier geboer, en as die grond verkoop is dan is dit nou klaar.

V/O:
Stefan’s father Coenie says a series of unfortunate events led to this situation – a prolonged drought, unsympathetic banks and unscrupulous money lenders targeting desperate farmers.
9
Mac:
Tell us about the drought. How bad was it and how long has it hit you for?

Coenie:
Mac, die droogte was baie lank gewees in Bultfontein van 2012 tot en met 2018 was dit baie droog.
V/O:
Unlike previous dry spells, this particular drought remained relentless for nearly a decade, which is extraordinary.
9
LINK:
The unprecedented drought cut a big swath across the central part of South Africa and severely affected many farmers in the Freestate and in the Northwest Province.
V/O:
In some years, no rain fell, and famers could not plant at all. It seems that the Bultfontein district in the Freestate, one of the country’s prime areas for white maize, was one of the hardest hit. And if farmers cannot plant, they have no source of income, and with no income, they get into trouble with those who extended credit to them – mainly the commercial banks.
24


Coenie:
En die oomblik as jy nie jou leuning diens nie is die Kriedietwet teen jou en dan begin die probleme.
V/O:
At the end 2020 into 2021 the drought in large parts of the Freestate was finally broken, and when we visited Bultfontein we saw bumper maize crops being harvested. But for many farmers, it is too late.

Annelien Joubert farms with cattle, maize, sunflower and peanuts. She agrees that the rain was not in time. 12
Annelien:
Dis te laat vir die banke, hulle het eintlik 2018 begin druk op die boere plaas, in die droogte en en jy het maar belowe en belowe en jy het skywe gemaak en jy het maar probeer kyk waar jy kan reg kom dat hulle jou kan help sodat jy kan plant. Maar van laas jaar af het hulle begin dagvaar en plase verkoop, boere meer tegemoet kom nie.
V/O:
Fourie senior has collected several auction signs to put on display …to symbolize the losses of so many farmers in Bultfontein. 12
Coenie:
My voorspelling aan die begin was dat 30% van Bultfontein se boere gaan hulle land verloor, en op die stadium staan ek op 36%.
LINK:
Each of these signs represents a farmer that no longer has their land, a family that does not have a home, and workers who are now unemployed.
V/O:
These are all farms that have been sequestrated in the greater Bultfontein District alone.

With no assistance forthcoming from Government, Agricultural Organizations or the Landbank, Fourie founded a Bultfontein Awareness Group that brought farmers, who shared the same plight, together. They organized days of prayer, and also, as a collective, tried to negotiate with creditors. The main credit provider to farmers in the Bultfontein area is First National Bank.
12


18
Coenie:
As so situasie wat ‘n “Act of God” is, ‘n ramp, ons tref, ek dink die banke kon hierdie situasie beter hanteer het ast dit hanteer is.
V/O:
This was a refrain we heard over and over again. While the farmers do not ascribe malice to FNB, they experience the bank as heartless and merciless, and this group of farmers told us they have been left with no saving, life insurance, annuities or medical aids.

Joubert says she found the bank really uncooperative.
Annelien:
Hulle stel ook nie rerig belang om met ons te onderhandel nie, of enigsins met ons vergaderings te hou, om te kyk hoe kan hulle die saak beredder nie. Daar is boere wat offers op die tafel te sit om hulle lenings en verbande te betaal en die bank het dit net afegeskiet.
V/O:
FNB responded that they were sympathetic towards the farmers:

As part our debt relief efforts, the Bank has had extensive engagements with farmers … The engagements resulted in the Bank entering into various leniency agreements, which resulted in the postponement of legal proceeding and auctions for a period of time. Legal proceedings will always be the last resort for the Bank .

However, several farmers also complained about what they say are excesses implemented by agents of the bank, such as the stationing of guards on sequestrated farms. 18



31

15

V/O:
FNB responded that:

There are instances where the Bank has a cession of crops, and where the liquidator has to ensure that the proceeds of a harvest are used as part of settling loan agreements.

The bank also says farmers are not prevented from harvesting crops, but the process is monitored for the benefit of creditors.

PD Botha who farms on the farm Salomosrus, felt violated by the way he says the bank treated him. When he experienced financial difficulties, he had rented out his land to another farmer to plant a crop of peanuts. 9



17


30
PD:
En die huurder se oes, is nie my oes nie, die grond is wel myne, maar nie die oes nie. En in Maartmaand was ek weg na my familie toe e nek het ‘n vriend gevra om asseblief tog net ‘n bietjie te kyk by die plaas of is alles oraait, en hy het my toe gebel om te se dat daar iemand is wat besig is om die grondboontjies uit te haal. Die was nie gereed om uitgehaal te word nie, dis drie weke te vroeg, hoekom het die persoon gewag tot ek nie daar is nie.
V/O:
We asked FNB about this incident and they replied:

FNB confirms that it has not appointed agents to harvest crops of farmers and/or third parties. Due to an ongoing legal process, we cannot provide any further information on this particular farm.

LINK:
With the banks refusing to extend any more credit to farmers in trouble, some of them out of sheer desperation are turning to alternative finance schemes, but are they legit?
V/O:
Annelien Joubert had heard about a company called Europlaw that offered financing to farmers based on a deal with an Ithuba Bank in the USA. Joubert applied for thirty million rand.
11
Annelien:
Die lening is toegestaan, maar jy moes ‘n persentasie van die bedrag waarvoor jy aansoek doen, moes jy betaal het, soos ‘n deposito om dit te kon ontvang.

Mac:
Hoeveel het julle betaal?

Annelien:
Ek het drie honderd duisend betaal. Daar is party boere wat een punt twee miljoen inbetaal het as a deposito.

Mac:
En toe, wat gebeur toe?

Annelien:
Niks gebeur nie. Hulle moes al in Oktober laasjaar uitbetaal het. Elke maand kom daar net ‘n brief wat dit uitstel.
V/O:
Alarmed, Joubert applied to Europlaw in May to have her three hundred thousand rand refunded, as per her contract. Europlaw has not responded to her request.

We contacted Europlaw and they answered us in several attorney’s letters, indicating that funds for the farmers have arrived from the US, and are currently in an unspecified local bank, though proof of payment has not yet been received. They also say they have sourced additional funds in the UK and that " the pay-outs are above board and in process to happen". Documentation can be viewed at their offices. They did not respond to questions about Joubert’s deposit.

We also tried several times to contact Ithuba Bank in US directly, without any success.

With many technical statements in Europlaw’s communication, we asked a leading forensic accountant, Johan Botha, for expert analysis.
5


7
Johan:
I went through all the correspondence that was sent to Carte Blanche and I tried to make sense of everything here, but it is almost impossible to find out what is going on. They promise all the time the money is almost there, it’s almost there, but there’s no money coming in. Be very, very careful, there is no guarantee and there is no money that I can see that is in South Africa, that will be paid out soon.
V/O:
The farmers also told us about several other non-traditional entities offering funding to desperate farmers. One of them is Community Chest Circles Association, that takes a deposit and a monthly fee from farmers. Amongst other things they offer farmers the opportunity to invest in silver coins. They also say that they are currently evaluating farmer’s business plans, and that no payments have been made yet.
30
LINK:
What is happening here in Bultfontein is not unique because of the prolonged drought many farmers all over South African also face liquidation and loss of their land.

V/O:
In fact, on the 20th of July the drought in large parts of the country was finally declared a national disaster, which compels various government agencies to implement contingency plans to assist farmers and the agricultural sector.

But for hundreds of farmers, it will come too late…this is certainly true for the Fouries.

Mac:
Oom Coenie is your son going to lose your family farm?

Coenie:
Ja, Mac. Stefan se seun sal die 7de geslag gewees het wat daar op daai plaas sou boer, end it is baie hartseer, maar dit is wat nou in Bultfontein gebeur en omliggend.

We contacted Europlaw and they answered us in several attorney’s letters, indicating that funds for the farmers have arrived from the US, and are currently in an unspecified local bank, though proof of payment has not yet been received. They also say they have sourced additional funds in the UK and that " the pay-outs are above board and in process to happen". Documentation can be viewed at their offices. They did not respond to questions about Joubert’s deposit. We also tried several times to contact Ithuba Bank in US directly, without any success. With many technical statements in Europlaw’s communication, we asked a leading forensic accountant, Johan Botha, for expert analysis. 5 7 Johan: I went through all the correspondence that was sent to Carte Blanche and I tried to make sense of everything here, but it is almost impossible to find out what is going on. They promise all the time the money is almost there, it’s almost there, but there’s no money coming in. Be very, very careful, there is no guarantee and there is no money that I can see that is in South Africa, that will be paid out soon. V/O: The farmers also told us about several other non-traditional entities offering funding to desperate farmers. One of them is Community Chest Circles Association, that takes a deposit and a monthly fee from farmers. Amongst other things they offer farmers the opportunity to invest in silver coins. They also say that they are currently evaluating farmer’s business plans, and that no payments have been made yet. 30 LINK: What is happening here in Bultfontein is not unique because of the prolonged drought many farmers all over South African also face liquidation and loss of their land. V/O: In fact, on the 20th of July the drought in large parts of the country was finally declared a national disaster, which compels various government agencies to implement contingency plans to assist farmers and the agricultural sector. But for hundreds of farmers, it will come too late…this is certainly true for the Fouries. Mac: Oom Coenie is your son going to lose your family farm? Coenie: Ja, Mac. Stefan se seun sal die 7de geslag gewees het wat daar op daai plaas sou boer, end it is baie hartseer, maar dit is wat nou in Bultfontein gebeur en omliggend.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: The story of a district where farmers are exploited to the maximum because they are in a financially vulnerable situation because of a 9-year-long drought.
metadata.Summary: In a huge area north of Bloemfontein (Bultfontein, Hoopstad, Wesselsbron) has had an incredibly severe drought for several years, and many farmers depleted all their reserves and got into serious financial trouble. The Government refused to help as did the various agricultural organizations. Many farmers now sit with a huge massive debt burden the vultures are circling, because there is a lot of money to be made – legally and illegally. The banks are foreclosing, all kinds of scamsters take advantage of farmers in financial trouble. Dozens of farmers have lost their family farms and for some the only way out is suicide.
metadata.Further information: HOW TO KICK A FARMER WHEN HE IS DOWN In a huge area North of Bloemfontein (Bultfontein, Hoopstad, Wesselsbron) has had an incredibly severe drought for several years, and many farmers depleted all their reserves, and got into serious financial trouble. The Government refused to help. Many farmers now sit with a huge massive debt burden the vultures are circling, because there is a lot of money to be made – legally and illegally. It is playing out in the following ways: • The major banks are liquidating farmers left right and centre. Then the farms are being sold for a fraction of their value. Christo Snyman farms and implements with a value of R40 million were sold for less than R10 million. The Banking Association of SA even told them that the banks got together and colluded to liquidate the farmers. FNB is in the forefront of all of this despite new legislation and prior promises and many meetings with people like Christo. In all of this liquidators and liquidating attorney in Bloemfontein are having a ball of a time. • A Bultfontein Awareness Committee was started in 2018 and negotiated with the banks, and despite concrete plans of how to save many farms and livelihoods, the pleas to the banks went unheeded. • Good rains fell last year and in a last-ditch effort to save themselves many farmers used private money to plant an the crops are looking promising. However, FNB has now stationed armed guards on many farms, to prevent farmers from harvesting crops, because they owe the bank money. They want to have it harvested themselves to sell. • Under the severe financial pressure, a number of farmers have committed suicide. • In recent months a number of unscrupulous characters and charlatans appeared with promises of financial assistance, and many farmers who are in danger of losing everything to the banks, fell for these schemes, losing more millions in the process. For example: o Ithuba Bank and Europlaw asked farmers 6% of every R100 000 they wanted to borrow as an admin fee. Some farmers paid between R1,6 mil and R1,8 mil in advance and the money in yet to arrive. o An evangelist, Louis Gerber of the Community Chests Circles Association got 1000 farmers to pay him R350 rand and R60 per month to get shares in the profit of the sale of 178 tons of gold which came into the country in 1965. The very same gold Tokyo Sexwale talked about. o Universal Venture Capital collected R3500 from farmers as an admin fee to obtains loans, but nothing happened. It seems it is a story of incredible hardship for a huge farming community and how banks and unscrupulous operators seem to be kicking them when they are down. Interviewees o Christo Snyman, who lost everything and who is the Chair of the Bultfontein Awareness Committee christo@teamgap.co.za o 2 other farmers who are in dire straits. o “Evangelist” Louis Gerber of the Community Chests Circles Association o Andre Vorster CEO of Europlaw or Hanno Bekker, manager at Europlaw o Coenie Fourie -- Bultfontein Awareness Committee
